key_insight: AIRRI makes educational text much harder for OCR and downstream LLM workflows by combining visual perturbations and adversarial attacks to reduce machine readability.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical testbed for designing and benchmarking machine-resistant document interfaces that preserve human readability while disrupting automated extraction.
method: Applies image-based perturbations: spacing changes, opacity variation, stripe overlays, and noise.
Uses decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA.
Evaluates against Tesseract, EasyOCR, and GOT-OCR2 using higher-education assignment text.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports large OCR degradation, including character error rate increases from 6.9% to 55.9% for EasyOCR and from 2.3% to 100.0% for Tesseract, with ADBA producing the strongest overall impact.
watch_item: Machine-resistant designs may trade off accessibility, visual quality, and robustness across different OCR systems, so human readability and real-world usability need careful validation.
paper_title: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
